blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Climate (temperature and rainfall) directly controls the rates of weathering and decomposition.
Organisms enrich soil quality—plants add humus while microbes break down organic matter.
Relief dictates soil depth, with steep slopes accelerating erosion and flat lands encouraging deep soil formation.
Parent material provides the fundamental mineral composition and texture of the soil.
Time is a critical passive factor, as mature soils take thousands of years to develop.

items: CLORPT stands for Climate, Organisms, Relief, Parent Material, and Time—frequently asked in multiple-choice questions.
Exam questions often contrast relief features: steep slopes lead to thin/eroded soils, whereas flat areas facilitate deep soil accumulation.
Parent material is tested as the primary determinant of a soil's initial texture and mineral profile.
